Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the line $y=\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}+2,$ and the lines $y=-x$ and $y=x,$ as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of the function $f(x,y)$ over the region $D$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type I regions.
feedback.worked_solution:
The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type I regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14082081/assets/47eccc29cbbdd917a247dec2f10329f718ed133b7e8398312b4ee3bc6bbbd647.png)

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le 0,\,-x\le y\le \sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}+2}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,x\le y\le \sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}+2}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{-x}^{\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}+2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{x}^{\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}+2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
